title: A Sigil for the Thorn
premise: Marguerite Quintana, a mercenary sworn to the silent god Vethra, has spent their whole life in Thornvale, a valley warded so that magic cannot enter or leave. When the wards collapse on the night the stars vanish, Marguerite discovers they carry Vethra's last living spark in their blood, and that the empire's witch-hunters will burn the valley to reclaim it. Guided by a defector hunter named Sable and the ragtag found family of the Thornvale garrison, Marguerite must choose between feeding the spark to the hunters' god-machine to save their people, or carrying it across the mountains to reignite Vethra and risk an ancient war. In the end, Marguerite splits the spark, giving half to the machine to buy peace and carrying half into exile, choosing love and found family over duty while accepting the war may come anyway.
about_author: Emrys Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oath-books before turning to fiction. They write from a farmhouse in the Welsh marches, where they keep bees and an unreasonable number of maps.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgot Magic
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A routine patrol along Thornvale's border wards establishes their life: mercenary work, quiet devotion to a god who stopped answering years ago, and the garrison family they've built. The emotional beat is restless contentment, the sense of a life balanced on something unseen.

chapters.title: Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Still Marguerite's POV. On watch, the stars go out one by one, then the border wards shatter like glass. Something crosses the boundary. Marguerite feels heat bloom under their skin for the first time in their life. The beat is dread and awe colliding.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were For
chapters.summary: Captain Ilsa Reyes POV. The garrison's aging captain reveals the valley's founding secret: the wards weren't built to keep magic out, but to hide something inside it. She looks at Marguerite when she says it. The beat is betrayal curdling into protectiveness.

chapters.title: The Hunter at the Gate
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A witch-hunter arrives under a parley banner, asking polite questions about 'anomalous births.' Sable, the hunter's reluctant tracker, senses the spark in Marguerite and says nothing. The beat is complicity beginning between enemies.

chapters.title: Blood Remembers
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Testing themselves alone in the hills, Marguerite accidentally kindles fire from bare air and hears Vethra's voice for the first time in fifteen years, fragmented and dying. The beat is terror transformed into longing.

chapters.title: Garrison Supper
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, rotating close-third among the garrison: cook Bram, scout Odile, young recruit Fen. A warm, funny dinner scene where each character reveals what Thornvale means to them, raising the stakes for what might be lost. The beat is found family made explicit.

chapters.title: Sable's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable privately warns Marguerite that the hunter, Inquisitor Corvane, already knows and is stalling only until reinforcements arrive. Sable offers passage over the mountains in exchange for help deserting. The beat is two people deciding to trust imperfectly.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Oath
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Flashback interwoven with present: thirty years ago, Ilsa helped bind Vethra's dying spark into a newborn child to keep the empire's god-machine fed and the valley forgotten. She confesses this to Marguerite. The beat is guilt meeting forgiveness neither can fully give.

chapters.title: Corvane Descends
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Reinforcements arrive; the inquisitor gives the garrison one day to surrender the 'vessel.' His chapters reveal the god-machine is starving and the empire will fracture without it. The beat is chilling, sympathetic fanaticism.

chapters.title: The Leaving
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite tries to slip away alone at night to spare the garrison; Fen catches them, and then the whole garrison does, insisting on coming. The beat is the found family refusing to let one member sacrifice alone.

chapters.title: First Blood on the Pass
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The company fights a rearguard skirmish against hunter outriders in the mountain pass. Bram is gravely wounded shielding Fen. The beat is the first real cost of the choice, grief sharpening resolve.

chapters.title: The God Beneath the Snow
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Sheltering in a shrine-ruin, Marguerite communes with Vethra properly and learns the truth: the god chose them willingly, and the 'ancient war' was the empire murdering every vessel before them. The beat is inheritance of a martyrdom.

chapters.title: Sable's Name
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable reveals their history: they were a valley child taken by the hunters, trained to hunt their own origin. Marguerite and Sable admit feelings neither can afford. The beat is love against duty stated plainly.

chapters.title: Fen's Choice
chapters.summary: Fen's POV. The youngest garrison member, captured briefly by scouts, lies convincingly about the company's route and escapes, proving their worth. But they saw the machine's hunger up close. The beat is coming-of-age through fear.

chapters.title: The Machine City
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. In the imperial capital, Corvane feeds prisoners to the failing god-machine and watches it reject them; only Vethra's spark can sustain it now. He begins to doubt whether he serves a god or a furnace. The beat is faith cracking.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Ford
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Corvane corners the company at a river crossing. Ilsa trades herself as a decoy so the others escape, marching into captivity with her old oath finally paid. The beat is sacrifice as redemption.

chapters.title: Vethra's Summit
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At the mountain shrine where Vethra died, the god offers Marguerite a choice: pour the whole spark back and be consumed, or split it. Marguerite realizes there may be a third path no one has dared. The beat is agency seized from prophecy.

chapters.title: Storming the Furnace
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation. The company, joined by deserters Sable recruited, assaults the machine-city to rescue Ilsa and confront Corvane. Fen and Odile hold the gate; Sable duels their former order. The beat is the found family at full strength.

chapters.title: A Sigil for the Thorn
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, climax. Before the machine and Corvane, Marguerite carves Vethra's sigil into their own chest and splits the spark: half into the starving machine to sustain it honestly, half kept within. Stars return overhead. The beat is self-definition over destiny.

chapters.title: What Corvane Saw
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Broken by the machine's whisper of gratitude, Corvane orders his hunters to stand down and turns himself over to imperial judgment rather than restart the purge. The beat is a fanatic's costly conversion.

chapters.title: Half a God
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Aftermath: Ilsa freed but stepping down, Bram mending, the valley's wards rebuilt differently, open instead of hiding. Marguerite and Sable choose each other openly. The beat is tenderness after ruin.

chapters.title: The Road Over the Mountains
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, closing. Marguerite leaves Thornvale carrying the living half-spark to find other silent gods, with Sable beside them and the garrison seeing them off. The final line acknowledges the war may come, and that they will meet it together. The beat is bittersweet hope.
